newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds finish strong week on steady note.
newsitem.headline: Bunds finish strong week on steady note.

text.p: Bund futures were steady in late trade after spending much of the day trading in positive territory thanks to strong overnight Treasuries.
The December DTB Bund contract was up one basis point in late trade at 100.26 after trading as high as 100.56 shortly after the open, a new high for the contract.
Trade was generally light with domestic German news having little impact on Bunds, including the release of a lower-than-expected tax revenue forecast for 1996 and 1997.
Dealers expect Bunds to remain generally firm, but in ranges through early next week.
The day ended what has been a strong week for Bunds with the futures contract smashing through an important psychological resistance point at 100.00.

Traders said the combination of weak manufacturing figures and higher-than-expected unemployment suggested that the German economy is not recovering as fast as had been expected, a positive sign for debt markets.

Many now expect the Bund contract to trade above 100.00 until the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday. Although the German economy is looking weak, fears of higher U.S. rates should keep a lid on Bunds.
